subject: Data processing locations and deletion timeline (follow-up)
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@bluewavehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueWave Health Legal <legal@bluewavehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: where your inference runs + deletion SLA

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — very helpful. As we move through procurement we have a couple of clarifying questions for our security and legal teams before we proceed to contract redlines:

1) For the hosted Redwood API, can you confirm the countries/regions where inference execution may occur? We need a short list of possible execution territories (region pairs are fine) and any conditions that would cause a request to be executed outside North America (e.g., capacity overflow, fallback routing).

2) Which subprocessors are involved in the inference path (both hosted API and Dedicated) and where those subprocessors have infrastructure located? We need an inventory that maps subprocessor -> country/region.

3) Deletion: if BlueWave issues an account-level erase request, what is the timeline for (a) removing customer data from active KV caches and request logs, (b) removing persisted logs/backups, and (c) evidence we provide to prove erasure to auditors? Please include any differences between hosted and Private (VPC/on-prem) options.

We'd like to consolidate answers into a short Q&A doc for Legal. If you have a one-page summary and a more detailed annex (subprocessor inventory and evidence checklist) that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if it's faster.

Best,
Ellen Park
Director of Platform Security
BlueWave Health

Attachments: none
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: where your inference runs + deletion SLA

Ellen — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short summary below and attached a two-part packet: a one-page residency+deletion summary and a CSV subprocessor inventory you can drop into your intake system. There are a few nuance items so I've looped in Jonas (infra) and Marissa (account lead) for any specifics you want added to the annex.

Executive summary (hosted API):
- Primary execution region: US (East & West) and EU (primary EU region is Frankfurt).
- Normal routing: requests from US customers are executed in US regions. EU customers can be pinned to EU-only execution when requested.
- Fallbacks that may cause cross-border execution: (a) capacity exhaustion in the pinned region, (b) regional outage/failover, or (c) explicit customer routing policy that allows burst to a compatible region. Such events are rare and we default to same-region execution where feasible.

Subprocessors (high-level):
- Cloud compute providers (dedicated GPU hosts): located in US, EU, APAC (listed in attached CSV with countries).
- Metrics & telemetry ingestion (for observability): hosted in US and EU; telemetry is sampled/minimized for PII.
- Key management integrations: customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own KMS (BYOK) via customer KMS integrations in supported regions.

Deletion and evidence:
- KV caches / active caches: cleared within seconds-to-minutes of an erase call for live state.
- Request logs / operational traces: soft-delete within 7 days (configurable retention window) and physical deletion from backups within 90 days for hosted API by default.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customers control retention and can opt for local-only logging; Redwood's control plane can still have metadata for billing but customers can request no-control-plane retention.
- Evidence: we provide a deletion certificate (signed JSON) with timestamps and checklist entries. For higher assurance, we can provide redacted logs showing sequence numbers of erased items and subprocessor attestation where available.

Attachments included:
- redwood-residency-summary.pdf (1-page)
- subprocessor-inventory.csv (detailed inventory)

Next steps: let us know if Legal wants the annex split into (A) evidence we can provide immediately and (B) items that require subprocessor attestations (may need 5–10 business days to gather). I'm happy to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the annex.

Cheers,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-residency-summary.pdf (pdf, 84 KB)
- subprocessor-inventory.csv (csv, 23 KB)

Thanks Sofia — that is really helpful. A couple follow-ups from Legal/Infra:  

- For the ‘‘fallbacks that may cause cross-border execution’’, can you quantify frequency historically (ballpark — e.g., <0.1% of requests, 1–2 outages per year that trigger cross-region fallback)? We need numbers for our risk assessment.

- For BYOK: if we provide a customer-managed key in AWS KMS eu-west-1, will any part of the encryption/decryption handshake leave eu-west-1? Legal is trying to understand whether key material or plaintext ever traverses outside the region.

- For the deletion certificate and subprocessor attestations: can you give an expected timeline for gathering attestations from cloud providers / metrics vendors (we are primarily concerned about third-party backups)?

If it helps, we can flag which questions require executive sign-off vs. those that are operational. Happy to take a call with Jonas if he prefers to share technical specifics.

Best,
Ellen

Ellen — thanks, happy to jump in with the technical details. Quick answers up front, full detail below.

1) Frequency of cross-region fallback: historically for customers pinned to a region we observe cross-region execution in <0.05% of requests (these are mostly short-term bursts when a pinned region hits sustained GPU pressure). Regional failovers that cause redistribution historically occur ~1–3 times per year across the entire fleet and are tied to maintenance or cloud provider incidents. We can provide a 12-month histogram for your team if that helps.

2) BYOK behavior: when customers use customer-managed KMS in eu-west-1, encryption/decryption of model context and short-lived artifacts happens via an integration that calls the customer KMS endpoint. Redwood does not export raw key material; the KMS handshake (Encrypt/Decrypt API calls) is made from compute nodes that are instantiated in the region you select. We will not route KMS calls through other regions for hosted customers pinned to EU-only. If the customer opts into cross-region burst routing, the BYOK policy will fallback to Redwood-managed KMS unless configured otherwise — we can document explicit behaviors for your legal team.

3) Subprocessor attestations and backup deletion timeline:
- Cloud providers (IaaS) typically have contractual deletion SLAs for snapshots and backups; in practice we expect physical removal of provider-managed snapshots within 30–90 days depending on provider.
- Observability/metrics vendors: attestation timelines vary; we can gather provider statements in ~7–10 business days for top-tier vendors and ~15 business days for smaller providers.
- Redwood evidence pack: for standard hosted customers we can deliver a deletion certificate within 3 business days of completion; subprocessor attestations (signed statements) are collected in parallel and will be appended to the evidence pack as they arrive.

Additional notes:
- Private/VPC deployments: you control the compute tenancy and can opt to keep all KMS and logs in-region; in that case Redwood does not have direct access to raw logs. Our control plane will still retain minimal billing metadata unless explicitly configured not to.
- Audit readiness: we recommend a short readiness run where we produce a sample deletion certificate + redacted log output for your auditors; this is often the fastest way to validate expectations. We can run that within 5 business days if you agree.

I've uploaded a technical annex to the shared folder with per-subprocessor country mappings and a small histogram of cross-region fallbacks for the past 12 months: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/residency-evidence-1478

If helpful, let's schedule a 30-minute technical call this week (I have availability Wed/Thu). Marissa — please advise on preferred times and whether BlueWave wants the annex as an NDA'ed bundle.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
